**Thursday, November 5, 2026 -**_****_

_**Iran:** Vice President JD Vance blames Republican election losses on Iran
war; Iran's Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf accuses U.S. of
putting Israel first. Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei says U.S. midterm
results will not change Washington's hostility toward Tehran. Iran says two
tankers, tugboat catch fire in Strait of Hormuz; UK reports tanker attacked
near Qatar. South Korea plans to expand naval mission near Strait of Hormuz.
U.S. sanctions Indian, Turkish firms over alleged ties to Iranian oil,
aviation. UAE airline profits plunge 66% amid Iran war._

_**Palestine:** Israeli attacks kill three Palestinians, including child, in
Gaza. Israeli settlers seize homes near Jericho, expelling Palestinians;
settlers say they are "dismantling the Oslo Accords." Israel demolishes five
buildings, displacing 105 Palestinians, and shuts down club in occupied East
Jerusalem. Israeli settlers burn olive trees, assault Palestinians as soldiers
demolish homes across the West Bank._

_**Yemen:** Saudi-led strikes kill around 20 across Yemen; Ansarallah shelling
kills woman, wounds five in Taiz. WSJ: Ansarallah demands recognition of
sovereignty over Yemen, $51 billion in compensation in exchange for halting
attacks on Saudi Arabia._

_**Lebanon:** Israeli strike kills one in southern Lebanon, again violating
ceasefire. Lebanon issues arrest warrants for two Hezbollah members over
seized explosives._

_**U.S.:** Democrats extend power in House, state races in latest midterm
election results. Exclusive: Civil-society groups propose delaying fight over
Iran war until 2027. CBS: Trump asks advisers if he should remove War
Secretary Pete Hegseth. NYT: SCOTUS justice Samuel Alito privately says he
won't retire immediately, despite Democrats' Senate win. House Speaker Mike
Johnson will not seek leadership role. Billionaire Leon Black sues Rep. Robert
Garcia for defamation over remarks about Epstein ties._

_**International:** World Health Organization approves Ebola vaccine trials
for dangerous Bundibugyo strain. Sudanese Army strike in North Kordofan kills
two women, destroys water station. Ethiopia, Sudan close each other's
consulates. Workers strike and march across France. Russian and Ukraine
exchange attacks; Russia kills four civilians in Donetsk. Syria secures $400+
million Saudi loan in new defense agreement. Stabbing attack outside Sri Lanka
embassy in Jordan kills security officer. Colombia expected to pass law
toughening terms of surrender for armed group, breaking with "total peace"
policy. UN elects five judges to International Court of Justice. Bomb threats
disrupt European air travel._

**This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday**

* * *

# Iran

  * **Vance blames Republican election losses on Iran war; Iran 's Ghalibaf accuses U.S. of putting Israel first: **The Iran war was the main reason Republicans lost the 2026 midterm elections, U.S. Vice President JD Vance [wrote](https://x.com/jdvance/status/2118004988433641835?a=LrzNrJAI749gFYGsuxg&s=46) on Thursday, arguing that voters who backed President Donald Trump in 2024 switched to supporting Democrats despite strong Republican turnout.

    * Citing private polling that he said accurately anticipated the results, Vance identified four leading reasons former Trump voters abandoned Republicans: "End the war," "Focus on cost of living/inflation," "Put America First," and "Change our relationship to Israel."

    * He said the findings vindicated calls for a diplomatic resolution to the conflict, and he warned against attributing the losses to the Trump administration's far-right immigration policies. "The reason we lost is the war. The president himself said so last night," Vance wrote. "If you'd like to argue it was worth it, that losing the Senate for the next 6 years was worth it, then do so."

    * Responding to Vance, Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf [accused](https://x.com/mb_ghalibaf/status/2118262614560047552?a=j0dzOsKjvfnrrQDhimQ&s=46) the Trump administration of preparing another phase of the conflict while prioritizing Israel over American interests. "Boss is prepping the next war phase while America teeters on an Israel-First cliff," Ghalibaf wrote, adding: "Why not say this to your boss?"

  * **Iran 's Khamenei says U.S. midterm results will not change Washington's hostility toward Tehran: **Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei said on Wednesday that anyone expecting a change in U.S. policy following Republican losses in the midterm elections is "seriously mistaken."

    * "Those who still harbor even the slightest hope that the behavior of the hegemonic system might change through partisan or factional shifts . . . are seriously mistaken," Khamenei said in a written statement published on his website.

  * **Iran says two tankers, tugboat catch fire in Strait of Hormuz; UK reports tanker attacked near Qatar:** Two oil tankers [caught fire](https://en.irna.ir/news/86313001/IRGC-Two-oil-tankers-tugboat-catch-fire-in-Strait-of-Hormuz) in separate incidents in the Strait of Hormuz after attempting to use "unauthorized" shipping routes, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Navy said on Thursday. A tugboat attempting to extinguish the fire also caught fire.

    * A tanker was struck by two unidentified projectiles approximately 50 nautical miles north of Madinat Al-Shamal, Qatar, the UK Maritime Trade Operations reported on Thursday. The condition of the crew and the extent of damage remain unconfirmed.

  * **South Korea plans to expand naval mission near Strait of Hormuz:** South Korea [plans](https://en.yna.co.kr/view/AEN20261105000751315) to expand its anti-piracy naval mission in the Gulf of Aden toward waters south of Oman, near the Strait of Hormuz, and deploy additional military assets, Yonhap reported on Thursday.

    * It would be Seoul's first military contribution to maritime security efforts in the region since the U.S.-Iran war began in February. In September, South Korea declined U.S. requests for direct military support against Tehran.

    * South Korean defense officials stressed that the mission would not involve combat forces and would remain independent of allied military operations. They said that aircraft will be prohibited from monitoring Iranian territory or entering the Strait of Hormuz.

  * **U.S. sanctions Indian, Turkish firms over alleged ties to Iranian oil, aviation:** On Wednesday, the U.S. Treasury Department [imposed](https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases/sb0681/) sanctions on individuals and companies in India and Turkey over their alleged support for Iran's oil and aviation sectors, as part of the Trump administration's Operation Economic Outcast campaign to restrict Iranian oil revenues during the war.

    * The Treasury Department accused Indian entities of falsifying vessel registrations for ships transporting Iranian oil. It also sanctioned Turkey-based Fugo Ground Services Inc. for supporting Iran's aviation sector.

    * The Treasury Department said last week that its sanctions campaign had contributed to the collapse of Iran's currency and increased inflation almost 90%.

  * **UAE airline profits plunge 66% amid Iran war:** The Dubai-based Emirates Group airline sustained a 66% decline in its after-tax profits, it [said](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/economy/emirates-groups-first-half-profit-plunges-66-amid-gulf-conflict-rising-fuel-costs/4112391) on Thursday. Year-on-year, the airline's profit fell to $1 billion in the first half of its 2026-27 financial year, as the Iran war disrupted air travel and pushed up fuel costs. The Emirates airline carried 21.8 million passengers between April and September, down 22% from a year earlier. The company said that it remained profitable despite the disruptions, with cash reserves declining to $14.7 billion by the end of September.

# Palestine

  * **Israeli attacks kill three Palestinians, including child, in Gaza:** Israeli forces [shot and killed](https://www.wafa.ps/news/2026/11/5/%D8%A7%D8%B3%D8%AA%D8%B4%D9%87%D8%A7%D8%AF-%D8%A7%D9%85%D8%B1%D8%A3%D8%A9-%D9%88%D8%B7%D9%81%D9%84-%D8%A8%D8%B1%D8%B5%D8%A7%D8%B5-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A7%D8%AD%D8%AA%D9%84%D8%A7%D9%84-%D9%81%D9%8A-%D8%AE%D8%A7%D9%86) a woman in Al-Mawasi, west of Khan Younis in southern Gaza, and a child in the Bureij refugee camp in central Gaza on Thursday, WAFA reported. Another Palestinian was killed in an Israeli airstrike west of Al-Zawayda in central Gaza.

  * **Israeli settlers seize homes near Jericho, expelling Palestinians; settlers say they are "dismantling the Oslo Accords": **Around 30 Israeli settlers, some of whom were armed, [took over](https://www.alaraby.co.uk/politics/%D9%8A%D8%AF%D9%8A%D8%B9%D9%88%D8%AA-%D8%A3%D8%AD%D8%B1%D9%88%D9%86%D9%88%D8%AA-%D9%85%D8%B3%D8%AA%D9%88%D8%B7%D9%86%D9%88%D9%86-%D9%8A%D8%B3%D8%AA%D9%88%D9%84%D9%88%D9%86-%D8%B9%D9%84%D9%89-8-%D9%85%D9%86%D8%A7%D8%B2%D9%84-%D9%82%D8%B1%D8%A8-%D8%A3%D8%B1%D9%8A%D8%AD%D8%A7) eight homes in Ein Al-Duyuk Al-Tahta on the outskirts of Jericho in the occupied West Bank on Wednesday. Activists warned that settlers could be reproducing the situation in Hebron, where armed Israeli settlers live in enclaves inside the Palestinian city, contributing to displacement and severe restrictions on Palestinian freedom of mobility. The operation near Jericho was organized by the Nachala settlement movement, which claims to have secretly purchased the properties.

    * Sixty-five Palestinian residents fled after settlers attacked them with stones, an activist [told](https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog_entry/after-settlers-enter-jericho-area-palestinian-residents-flee-homes-say-they-are-afraid-to-return/) the Times of Israel. Residents said that Israeli forces subsequently blocked access to the area, leaving homeowners afraid to return.

    * The new outpost is reportedly located in Area C, under full Israeli control under the Oslo Accords, just meters from parts of Jericho classified as Area A, where the Palestinian Authority is supposed to exercise civilian and security control.

    * Yisrael Gantz, head of the West Bank settler council, framed the move as an effort to dismantle the Oslo Accords, declaring: "Today we begin reversing the trend, dismantling the Oslo Accords through actions, house by house, family by family."

    * Palestinian National Council Speaker Rawhi Fattouh condemned the takeover as "organized terrorism" carried out under Israeli government protection, charging Israel of encouraging settlement expansion and forced displacement.

  * **Israel demolishes five buildings, displacing 105 Palestinians, and shuts down club in occupied East Jerusalem:** Israeli forces [demolished](https://www.facebook.com/jergover/videos/%D8%AA%D8%AD%D8%AF%D9%8A%D8%AB-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A7%D8%AD%D8%AA%D9%84%D8%A7%D9%84-%D9%8A%D9%87%D8%AF%D9%85-5-%D9%85%D8%A8%D8%A7%D9%86%D9%8D-%D8%B3%D9%83%D9%86%D9%8A%D8%A9-%D9%81%D9%8A-%D8%A8%D9%84%D8%AF%D8%A9-%D8%A8%D8%AF%D9%88-%D9%88%D9%8A%D8%B4%D8%B1%D9%91%D8%AF-105-%D9%85%D9%88%D8%A7%D8%B7%D9%86%D9%8A%D9%86%D8%A5%D8%B9%D9%84%D8%A7%D9%85-%D9%85%D8%AD%D8%A7%D9%81%D8%B8%D8%A9-%D8%A7%D9%84%D9%82/1419075760284494/) five residential buildings containing 12 apartments in the town of Biddu, northwest of occupied East Jerusalem, on Thursday, displacing 105 Palestinians without prior warning, citing construction without permits. Soldiers fired stun grenades and tear gas at residents and prevented families from removing their belongings before demolishing their homes, according to the Jerusalem Governorate.

    * Separately, Israeli authorities shut down the Abna Al-Quds Club in Jerusalem's Old City under an order issued by National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir. The governorate condemned both measures as part of an escalating Israeli campaign targeting Palestinian homes, institutions, and community life in Jerusalem.

  * **Israeli settlers burn olive trees, assault Palestinians as soldiers demolish homes across the West Bank:**

    * **Ramallah:** Israeli settlers [set fire](https://www.wafa.ps/news/2026/11/5/%D9%85%D8%B3%D8%AA%D8%B9%D9%85%D8%B1%D9%88%D9%86-%D9%8A%D8%B6%D8%B1%D9%85%D9%88%D9%86-%D8%A7%D9%84%D9%86%D8%A7%D8%B1-%D9%81%D9%8A-%D8%A3%D8%B4%D8%AC%D8%A7%D8%B1-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B2%D9%8A%D8%AA%D9%88%D9%86) to dozens of centuries-old olive trees in the village of Burqa, east of Ramallah, on Thursday, according to WAFA.

    * **Jericho:** Three Palestinians were [injured](https://www.wafa.ps/news/2026/11/5/%D8%A5%D8%B5%D8%A7%D8%A8%D8%A9-3-%D9%85%D9%88%D8%A7%D8%B7%D9%86%D9%8A%D9%86-%D8%A8%D8%A7%D8%B9%D8%AA%D8%AF%D8%A7%D8%A1-%D9%85%D8%B3%D8%AA%D8%B9%D9%85%D8%B1%D9%8A%D9%86-%D8%B9%D9%84%D9%8A%D9%87%D9%85-%D9%81%D9%8A) after settlers, accompanied by Israeli forces, raided Palestinian homes in the Bedouin communities of Ard Satih, west of Jericho, beating residents and spraying them with pepper spray.

    * **Nablus:** Settlers [attacked](https://www.wafa.ps/news/2026/11/5/%D8%A5%D8%B5%D8%A7%D8%A8%D8%A9-%D9%85%D9%88%D8%A7%D8%B7%D9%86-%D9%86%D8%AA%D9%8A%D8%AC%D8%A9-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A7%D8%B9%D8%AA%D8%AF%D8%A7%D8%A1-%D8%B9%D9%84%D9%8A%D9%87-%D8%A8%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B6%D8%B1%D8%A8-%D9%85%D9%86) farmers in Beita, south of Nablus, injuring one Palestinian. Israeli forces also demolished a home in Furush Beit Dajan, east of Nablus.

    * **Salfit:** Israeli forces [demolished](https://www.wafa.ps/news/2026/11/5/%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A7%D8%AD%D8%AA%D9%84%D8%A7%D9%84-%D9%8A%D8%B4%D8%B1%D8%B9-%D8%A8%D9%87%D8%AF%D9%85-%D9%85%D9%86%D8%B2%D9%84-%D9%88%D9%8A%D8%AE%D8%B7%D8%B1-%D8%A8%D9%88%D9%82%D9%81-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A8%D9%86%D8%A7%D8%A1) a home in Qarawat Bani Hassan and issued a stop-work order for another home. Three Palestinians were also injured in assaults by Israeli soldiers and settlers in the town.

# Yemen

  * **Saudi-led strikes kill around 20 across Yemen; Ansarallah shelling kills woman, wounds five in Taiz:** Saudi-led coalition bombardment killed around 20 people across the Yemeni governorates of Al-Jawf, Al-Bayda, Saada, and Taiz over the past 24 hours, according to Ansarallah-affiliated media. Ansarallah military spokesman Yahya Saree said that the coalition carried out 104 attacks across areas controlled by the group, including the capital, Sana'a.

    * Meanwhile, Yemen's Saudi-backed government reported that Ansarallah shelling in Taiz killed a woman and wounded five people.

  * **WSJ: Ansarallah demands recognition of sovereignty over Yemen, $51 billion in compensation in exchange for halting attacks on Saudi Arabia:** Yemen's Ansarallah [demanded](https://www.wsj.com/world/middle-east/saudi-arabia-has-no-easy-choices-as-it-weighs-how-to-combat-houthi-threat-a4adc358) $51 billion in compensation for years of Saudi airstrikes and blockade and formal recognition as Yemen's sovereign power in exchange for halting attacks on Saudi Arabia, the Wall Street Journal reported. Riyadh reportedly approached the group after Ansarallah attacks on Saudi oil tankers in the Red Sea and territorial advances near the strategic Bab al-Mandab Strait.

    * Saudi officials told the WSJ that Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman is reluctant to negotiate without military leverage but fears that deploying additional ground troops could result in heavy casualties. The UAE's withdrawal from the anti-Ansarallah campaign, Washington's refusal to provide direct military support, and Saudi's reliance on regional allies further complicated Riyadh's options, the report said.

# Lebanon

  * **Israeli strike kills one in southern Lebanon, again violating ceasefire:** An Israeli drone strike killed one person and wounded another in Qabrikha, in the Marjeyoun district of southern Lebanon, on Wednesday, Lebanon's National News Agency reported. The Israeli military [said](https://x.com/idf/status/2118011077547954254?a=VWpvX6fJy--rbGH3t7Q&s=46) that it targeted two people who were "observing" its forces in the area, without providing any evidence that the individuals were military targets.

    * Separately, Israeli warplanes [carried out](https://www.nna-leb.gov.lb/ar/news/572426/%D8%BA%D8%A7%D8%B1%D8%AA%D8%A7%D9%86-%D9%84%D9%84%D8%B9%D8%AF%D9%88-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A5%D8%B3%D8%B1%D8%A7%D8%A6%D9%8A%D9%84%D9%8A-%D8%AA%D8%B3%D8%AA%D9%87%D8%AF%D9%81%D8%A7%D9%86-%D8%B7%D9%84%D9%88%D8%B3%D8%A9-%D9%88%D9%85%D8%AD%D9%8A%D8%B7%D9%87%D8%A7-2) two airstrikes on Tallousa and its outskirts in the Marjeyoun district, and struck the outskirts of Aita al-Jabal in the Bint Jbeil district.

  * **Lebanon issues arrest warrants for two Hezbollah members over seized explosives:** Lebanon's Military Court issued arrest warrants for two Hezbollah members in connection with the seizure of 780 kilograms (1,720 pounds) of explosives at the Dahr Al-Baydar checkpoint linking Beirut to the Bekaa Valley, the National News Agency reported.

    * The explosives were seized last month. Lebanese authorities indicted 13 people in the case, on charges involving state security, illegal possession of weapons and explosives, and forming unlawful organizations. Beyond the two Hezbollah members, the remaining 11 defendants are still at large. The government's attempt to question six defendants was postponed following an objection filed by their lawyer.

# U.S. News

  * **Democrats extend power in House, state races in latest midterm election results:** Additional races were called on Wednesday, extending Democrats' commanding lead in the House of Representatives and in state-level posts. Senate elections in Mississippi and Alaska remain uncalled as of Thursday morning, while an unexpectedly tight Senate race in Louisiana was called in favor of the Republican, **Julia Letlow.**

    * **Sam Forstag,** a labor union leader and smokejumper endorsed by Rep. **Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez** , won his election to represent Montana's first congressional district, a seat previously held by Trump's former Interior Secretary, **Ryan Zinke**. Forstag is the first Democratic candidate to win a congressional race in the state since former Sen. **Jon Tester** won in 2018. He is also the youngest congressional representative from the state since the 1930s.

    * Progressive activist **William Lawrence** officially [ousted](https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2026-election/william-lawrence-democrat-michigan-house-election-win-tom-barrett-rcna603374) Republican incumbent **Tom Barrett** in Michigan's seventh congressional district. Lawrence, a co-founder of the Sunrise Movement, won one of the most competitive elections this cycle by emphasizing the rising cost of living in Michigan, opposing data centers, calling for restrictions on Flock cameras, and pushing for tighter regulation of artificial intelligence.

    * Republican incumbent Rep. **Max Miller** , who was accused of physical and verbal abuse by his ex-wife, conceded defeat to Democrat **Brian Poindexter** in Ohio's seventh congressional district, which covers much of the Cleveland suburbs.

    * Progressive **Angela Gonzales-Torres** defeated incumbent Democrat Rep. **Jimmy Gomez** in California's 34th congressional district. The 31-year-old was backed by Justice Democrats and the Los Angeles chapter of the Democratic Socialists of America in her May primary against the AIPAC-backed Gomez.

    * Two other races featuring progressives in California have yet to be called. **Mai Vang** , a progressive from the Sacramento area, trails incumbent **Doris Matsui** by 15 points with less than half of the vote counted. **Aisha Wahab** , a progressive who won a special election to fill the northern California seat vacated by **Eric Swalwell** , leads her opponent, **Melissa Hernandez,** by 13 points, with just over half of the votes counted.

    * **Nithya Raman** , whose Los Angeles City Council campaigns were boosted by the local D.S.A. chapter, [defeated](https://thehill.com/homenews/state-watch/6149517-nithya-raman-los-angeles-mayor/) incumbent Mayor **Karen Bass** in a contentious race. Los Angeles's D.S.A. chapter endorsed her candidacy for mayor, despite Raman's acceptance of an endorsement from a pro-Israel group and lack of clarity on whether she supports the Boycott, Divestment, Sanctions movement. Raman maintains that she was an early advocate for a ceasefire in Gaza, and has characterized Israel's conduct in Gaza as a genocide. The national D.S.A. narrowly voted against rescinding the Los Angeles chapter's endorsement.

  * **Civil-society groups propose delaying fight over Iran war until 2027:** A draft letter circulating among civil-society organizations, a copy of which was obtained by Drop Site Daily, initially proposed punting on the critical fight over war funding until 2027. After Drop Site approached the groups who had signed, the letter was adjusted to be more forceful. The background: Funding for the government expires on December 11, 2026. [Sen. ](https://x.com/davidsirota/status/2117783546488402277?a=igSLLIXz8xdw-GvWwnw&s=20)**[Chris Van Hollen](https://x.com/davidsirota/status/2117783546488402277?a=igSLLIXz8xdw-GvWwnw&s=20)**[ ](https://x.com/davidsirota/status/2117783546488402277?a=igSLLIXz8xdw-GvWwnw&s=20)and Rep. **Ro Khanna** have proposed using that date as leverage to force an end to the war, not through a war powers resolution--which Trump has already ignored--but by legally barring the government from spending money on the war. Instead, the groups signing the letter proposed focusing on measures that have no bearing on the administration's ability to prosecute the war. The letter read:

    * "In Tuesday's elections, people across the United States made their will resoundingly clear: they want to end President Trump's war on Iran, its resulting violence, and its downstream economic hardship, immediately. Ending this war cannot wait."

    * "We, the XX undersigned civil society organizations, urge you to respond to this mandate _by voting down any defense authorization or defense appropriations bills that would continue funding this disastrous war or increase Pentagon funding beyond the already outrageous $1 trillion_ that the White House pushed through Congress last year" (emphasis added).

    * _But:_**** Congress has no plans to fund the war through a defense appropriations bill. The plan is to pass a continuing resolution on or before December 11. So far, signatories to the draft letter include the Center for International Policy Advocacy, Indivisible, J Street, MoveOn, National Iranian American Council Action, and Win Without War. The letter went on: "_If Trump continues the war into the new year, we further urge returning members to prioritize and pass legislation expressly defunding this war early in the new Congress._ " Such an approach would let Trump have November and December to wage war before _" expressly defunding this war early in the new Congress."_**** That line is being stripped out, sources said.

    * **Matt Duss** , executive director of CIPA, one of the signatories, emphasized his support for the more aggressive approach proposed by Van Hollen. "Congress needs to use every tool it has right now to stop this war," he said. "We want everyone to be going all the way."

    * At issue is the question of just how hard Democrats should fight Trump's war. Not every group involved, sources said, was yet convinced to take the approach called for by Duss and Van Hollen, despite the resounding mandate.

  * **CBS: Trump asks advisers if he should remove War Secretary Pete Hegseth:** Trump is [asking](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/trump-hegseth-midterm-election-losses/) his advisers if he should remove War Secretary **Pete Hegseth** from his post, CBS News reported on Wednesday, suggesting that the president is searching for a scapegoat after the Republican Party suffered historic election losses driven by voter anger over the Iran war. Some aides predict that blame will fall on U.S. military Commander Adm. **Brad Cooper** , the head of Central Command, and the Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, Gen. **Dan Caine**. Florida Gov. **Ron DeSantis** is being floated as a replacement for Hegseth. If Hegseth is replaced, he may try to take up the Tennessee Senate seat that **Marsha Blackburn** is vacating to become governor. Trump has told reporters that Hegseth would be "very popular" as a senator.

  * **NYT: SCOTUS justice Samuel Alito privately says he won 't retire immediately, despite Democrats' Senate win**: The Supreme Court Justice Samuel Alito privately says he intends to remain on the bench after Democrats swept the Senate, two people close to Alito [told](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/04/us/politics/alito-trump-supreme-court-not-retiring.html) the New York Times. His announcement follows speculation that he or Justice Clarence Thomas might retire during the lame-duck session. Some experts speculate that outgoing Republican senators--such as John Cornyn, Bill Cassidy, or Susan Collins--might try to help Trump push a new SCOTUS nominee through the confirmation process.

  * **House Speaker Mike Johnson will not seek leadership role:** Following the Democratic takeover of the House of Representatives, Speaker**Mike Johnson** told staff on Wednesday he will not [seek](https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/congress/house-speaker-mike-johnson-republican-leader-gop-losses-rcna607434) the minority leader post in the new Congress.

    * After the news broke, House Majority Leader **Steve Scalise**[proposed](https://www.politico.com/live-updates/2026/11/04/congress/steve-scalise-minority-leader-01149152) a "consensus-driven" bid for the Minority Leader position, saying that the election "was far worse than any of us expected." He will [face](https://www.foxnews.com/politics/jim-jordan-throws-hat-ring-house-minority-leader-gop-picks-up-pieces-after-blue-wave) Judiciary Chairman **Jim Jordan** , who also announced a bid to become House Minority Leader on Wednesday, touting his "battle-testing" in oversight hearings and his readiness to counter Democratic investigations. Republicans will vote for new leadership on November 10.

    * Rep. **Tom Emmer**(R-Minn.)**,** the current Majority Whip and the presumptive Minority Whip, [faces](https://abcnews.com/Politics/live-updates/midterm-elections-live-updates?id=137782085&entryId=137864011&gsid=bb3b0397-dc32-4595-a192-7fd31fc66ab5) a challenge from Rep. **August Pfluger**(R-Texas)**,** ABC News reported on Wednesday. Emmer told colleagues in a letter that he took Tuesday's failures "personally" and could not "sugarcoat" Republican defeats. Pfluger, for his part, promoted his ability to make "the changes" the caucus would need to win in 2028.
